key_insight: PathFM turns forecasting into full trajectory generation, using flow matching plus distillation to produce multiple plausible future paths quickly and with better path-level calibration.
engineering_relevance: This is useful when downstream decisions depend on path shape and dependence structure, such as cumulative demand, peak load, event timing, and risk-sensitive planning.
method: Uses flow matching to generate complete future trajectories instead of only marginal quantiles.
Distills the sampler to one or two steps and reuses history attention cache across draws for fast multi-sample forecasting.
Adds a direct calibration-loss optimization path made practical by the fast distilled sampler.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports competitive marginal accuracy on fev-bench and TIME, and higher aggregate path score on the new fps-bench than all evaluated external baselines, with chaotic-system tests showing stronger long-run variability retention.
watch_item: The fast sampler and calibration benefits may depend on careful distillation and cache-sharing implementation, so stability and reproducibility should be checked on new datasets and longer horizons.
paper_title: PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting of Multivariate Trajectories
